Antineoplastics may be used during pregnancy for their immunosuppressant properties in auto-immune disease, and for the treatment of cancer, which can complicate 1 in 1000 pregnancies.1-3 Although the use of potentially teratogenic drugs would normally be avoided during pregnancy, the risk to the mother of inadequate treatment may outweigh whatever risks ex- ist of abnormality in the fetus.1 The highest incidence of adverse effects appears to occur after exposure during the first trimester:1-4 about 10 to 20% of fetuses exposed to cytotoxics during this period have major malforma- tions, compared with 3% in the general population.1 Malforma- tions reflect the gestational age at exposure. The fetus is particu- larly vulnerable when exposed during organogenesis (weeks 2 to 8 after conception), and the heart, neural tube, and limbs are af- fected earlier than the palate and ear; after organogenesis, the eyes, genitalia, haematopoietic system, and CNS remain vulner- able to continued exposure.3 The risk of fetal malformations after exposure during the second and third trimesters is probably no higher than the background rate, but there may still be an increased risk of still-birth, fetal growth restriction, premature birth, and maternal or fetal myelo- suppression.1-3 The delayed effects of antineoplastics on development have not been well-documented. Despite concerns that premature birth and low birth-weight could contribute to retardation of growth, development, and intellect,5 long-term follow-up of a limited number of children has not shown any evidence of abnormali- ties.3-5 Similarly, although maternal antineoplastic therapy has been implicated in a case of childhood neuroblastoma and papil- lary thyroid cancer, the child’s fraternal twin, exposed to the same drugs in utero, was healthy.3 There have been no reports of secondary leukaemias in exposed offspring, but the longer term risk is unknown.3 The teratogenicity of any drug depends on the timing of expo- sure, the dose, and the characteristics affecting placental trans- fer,3 as well as the actions of the drug.
